pattern: Show the thing working: a 15-120 s screen-recording/demo video with a 1-3 line outcome caption is the biggest reach lever for product posts
how_to_apply:
Template: '[What it does, as an outcome or a what-if].

[One line: how it works / built with what].

[Who you built it with or what inspired it].' + attach a 15-60 s screen recording of [Curio doing the thing] - first frame already mid-action, no logo intro. Use whenever a feature visibly works (new screen, AI answer, mobile build running). Avoid: posting the same demo again as an 'update' the next day (1.05x), and caption-only reactions to your own video without a contrast or number (0.47x).

pattern: Unexpected result + the cause + 'No X. No Y.' + one-line takeaway (result_first with a real number) out-reaches plain milestones 5-15x
how_to_apply:
Template: '[Thing you did] [when].

[Surprising result with an exact small number].

No [usual effort 1].
No [usual effort 2].
No [usual effort 3].

Just [the actual cause].

[One-line takeaway other builders can steal].' Attach the proof as a simple chart/screenshot (before vs after). Works at tiny scale: '0 to 37 waitlist signups in 2 days. No launch. No ads. Just [X].' Avoid plain milestones with no cause or lesson ('crossed 150 stars!' = 0.73x, '10,000 downloads' = 0.61x).

pattern: One-line contrarian take on the builder world's own habits or tools (under ~25 words, no link, no image needed) reliably beats the median and pulls replies
how_to_apply: Templates: '"[popular phrase]" has mostly been [what people actually do]. that's not [X]. that's [Y].' / '[Common growth tactic] might be the worst [thing] ever invented.' / 'Dear @[tool], please [tiny specific fix].' / sarcastic 'How to [goal] in 1 minute: 1. [bad practice] 2. … — [named culprit]. What's the best alternative?' Pick a take you'd defend in replies and that comes from building Curio. End with a question when you want replies (228 replies on 66). Avoid generic praise of a tool (0.22x).

pattern: Image-led post: a screenshot, meme or before/after with a 5-12 word caption lets the image carry the story and spreads by reposts/bookmarks
how_to_apply: Template: '[≤12-word reaction or setup]' + [one image that makes sense in 1 second: a screenshot of a user's message/result, a before vs after of a Curio screen with dates as labels, or a niche meme about building with AI]. Use 2-3x/week between demo and text posts. Two of the four winners were off-topic (memes, fitness) - keep the image about building Curio. Avoid long captions that repeat the image.

pattern: Keep links and asks out of the post body: winners give first and put 'try it' / repo links in a self-reply; posts with a URL or upvote/LIVE ask in the body sit at 0.3-0.8x
how_to_apply: Post body = hook + proof (video/image) + takeaway, no URL. Then reply to yourself: 'try it here: [curioapp.online]' (alexcooldev's link replies still got 1-4K views). Asks ('give us a star', 'join the waitlist') go after the value, without a URL in the body. Avoid: 'LIVE: … [link]' (0.34x), 'Upvotes appreciated [PH link]' (0.78x), '[demo] on [yourproduct.com]' (0.47x).

pattern: One-stop reference map of a whole sub-field (gallery, 'N architectures with when-to-use', free bundle/cheat sheet) — avg 2.17x creator median REACTIONS (not views; LinkedIn has no public views)
how_to_apply: Template: line 1 = '[N] [THINGS] every [AUDIENCE] should know: ([explained with when to use each])' or 'I put together [ONE PLACE] for [ALL OF X] so you stop [PAIN]'. Body: numbered list, each item = name → what it does (1 line) → when to use it (1 line). One diagram/cover that shows the whole map (doc carousel for the owner: 1 item per page). Use for: RAG variants, attention variants, positional encodings, fine-tuning methods, eval metrics, reasoning techniques. Avoid: recap lists of your own old posts (Akshay '9/12 concepts' recaps = 0.95-1.0x), narrow single-metric tables (Raschka MoE table 0.47x), comment-gated giveaways (76 had 7.8x comments from gating — don't copy). Medium not high: 76's numbers partly giveaway mechanics.

pattern: Contrarian reframe of a hyped AI component ('Many engineers think [X] is the system. It's quietly becoming the least important part') then pay it off with an architecture — avg 3.07x creator median REACTIONS
how_to_apply: Template (first 2 lines, before see-more, <210 chars): 'Many engineers think [HYPED THING] is [WHAT MATTERS]. But it's quietly becoming [THE LEAST IMPORTANT PART]...' or '[NEW DISCIPLINE] will be one of the most important [FIELD] skills of the next decade. Here's why...'. Then: 'Here's the architecture:' + 3 layers. Must be backed by a concrete example the reader uses (Claude Code, Cursor). For research posts: '[POPULAR BELIEF about a paper/technique] is wrong. [PAPER] shows [NUMBER].' Low confidence: all 3 posts are one creator (Paul Iusztin, 113K). Test 2-3 times before relying on it.

pattern: Numbered layer/step breakdown: claim → 'Here's the architecture:' → 1/ 2/ 3/ bold-header sections, each = what it is + bullets + one opinion → payoff line — avg 3.05x creator median REACTIONS
how_to_apply: Structure for a 1,500-2,500 char text post (or doc carousel, one section per page): [HOOK CLAIM] / 'Here's the [architecture|pipeline|recipe]:' / '1/ [LAYER NAME]' + 3-5 bullets + 'I prefer [CHOICE] because [REASON]' / '2/ …' / '3/ …' / closing line: '[WHAT THIS MEANS FOR YOU]'. One line per idea, white space. Pair with a single diagram of the layers. Works for: how a paper's method works (stages), how a model is trained (pretrain → SFT → RL), how an agent stack fits together. Raschka's paper breakdowns use the same idea with 🔹 headers (HRM→TRM 1.48x, his best paper breakdown).

pattern: Personal quest + tiny concrete number ('For years I tried to understand [X]… built the smallest one: 16 parameters' / 'I just built [X] running 100% locally') — avg 1.75x creator median REACTIONS
how_to_apply: Template: 'For [TIME] I've been trying to understand [CONCEPT] my way. So I built the smallest [THING] I could: [TINY NUMBER — 4 words, 16 parameters, 1 GPU-hour].' or 'I just built [SYSTEM] ([CONSTRAINT: 100% local / under $5 / 200 lines]).' Then: what surprised me → how it works (3-4 steps) → code/notebook in first comment. Great fit for a starting account: needs no audience or authority, only a real experiment. Contrast: the SAME Serrano content posted as 'The world's smallest transformer is out!' got 0.51-0.59x.

pattern: Lead with the idea, not the release: 'video/part N is out', 'updated version', 'last of the trilogy' posts flop (0.29-0.59x); the same content framed as the insight wins (1.68-1.78x) — creator median REACTIONS
how_to_apply: Never open with '[ASSET] is out!', 'Part [N] of…', 'Updated version of…'. Open with the finding the asset contains: '[SURPRISING RESULT] — here's how' and put the link in the first comment. Series: make every post stand alone (no 'second in a trilogy' in line 1). Flop evidence (not linked as evidence because they are below 1.5x): posts 109 (0.59x), 111 (0.51x) Serrano; 114 (0.29x) Grootendorst Mamba update; 112 (0.47x) Raschka table. Low confidence: winners from one creator.

pattern: The finished, working thing is in frame 1 with a one-line 'I made/built [X] that [does Y]' on screen — the build process comes after (or never)
how_to_apply: First frame = the result running/in your hand (app on the phone, dashboard live, gadget working), text overlay ≤10 words: 'I built [THING] that [SURPRISING JOB]' or 'Would you use this [THING] I made? It [DOES Y]'. Then (optional) how: problem → steps → result again. Use for every Curio feature reveal. Avoid: opening on your face explaining, logos, or 'Day N' alone. Follow-ups of the same build decay (0.44-0.51x) — post the first reveal as the strongest cut.

pattern: Build-for-my-own-life framing: feed the AI/your build a real, personal input (my bank statements, my wall, my fiancé, my team's paid tools) and show a concrete personal number in the result
how_to_apply: Template: 'I gave [MODEL/TOOL] [MY REAL DATA: N years of X / N files] and asked for [OUTPUT]. [TIME] later: [RESULT]. [ONE PERSONAL NUMBER: I went to X 92 times].' Or: 'I cancelled [N] subscriptions because I built [REPLACEMENT] in [HOURS] — [TOOL] was costing me [$/month].' For Curio: show it on the owner's own reading/learning history. Show the exact prompt on screen (save-bait). Avoid generic demo data.

pattern: 'Impossible build' claim with a famous reference + a time/prompt constraint, proven by the thing running: '[GTA-6 / Call of Duty / any SaaS] in [one prompt / a few hours]'
how_to_apply: Hook: 'I built [FAMOUS THING EVERYONE KNOWS] in [ONE PROMPT / N HOURS] with [NEW MODEL]' over the running result. Time it to a model release or a trending reference (GTA-6 news, a new Claude/GPT). Show the prompt for 1-2 s. Avoid stale references: 'Smash Bros in 1 prompt' (0.95x) and '4 builders 1 Mario Kart prompt' (0.67x) didn't land — the reference must be hot this week.

pattern: ≤15 s silent or near-silent single-shot loop with one text line (question or year/role label) — rewatch bait that beat 30-60 s talking heads by 5-150x
how_to_apply: Make 1 in 3 reels a 6-12 s clip: one take, no voiceover, music/ambient, one line of text on screen the whole time. Two templates: (a) object/app working + 'Would you use this [X] I made?'; (b) dev skit with label 'Software engineers in [YEAR]:' and a twist on the last shot (2027 = empty chair). End on a frame that loops into the first. Avoid: 30-40 s selfie career/opinion takes (0.17-0.4x for the same creator).

pattern: Release-week hook: name the new model in the first line + a reaction ('[MODEL] is wild / just came out'), then show what you built with it
how_to_apply: Within 72 h of a major model release: '[NEW MODEL] just came out and I [BUILT/REPLACED X] in [TIME]' + red label '[MODEL] is wild' on the result. Only with a real build to show; one creator so far (Riley Brown, 2.5-4x) — test it, don't make it the default.

pattern: Surprising-truth hook about a tool the viewer already uses (a stat or 'everyone is doing X wrong') + proof on screen in the first 2 s + a free fix they can apply in 30 s
how_to_apply: Line 1: '[TOOL] [does surprising thing] [N]% of the time - even when [you're wrong / it looks fine].' or 'Everyone's [paying for / overcomplicating] [X]; all you need is [simple thing].' Frame 1: your face + a 6-9 word title box '[How to force TOOL to STOP X]'; by 1-2 s pop the receipt (study screenshot, error, setting). Then 'Here's how to fix it in 30 seconds:' -> exact click path / prompt -> one bonus trick -> 'comment [WORD] for the full prompt'. Use for AI Explained episodes about ChatGPT/Claude behaviour (sycophancy, hallucination, context rot, model choice). Avoid: same topic with a bare caption and no claim (mavgpt's twin post did 4.2K vs 386K).

pattern: Explain the confusing thing beginners literally see in the product (model picker, plugin/skill/MCP menu, a named error) with one analogy ladder and one everyday example per option
how_to_apply: Open on the UI element itself (screenshot of the dropdown/menu) + 'X, Y and Z - what's the difference and when do you use each?'. Then ONE analogy ladder ([X] = middle schooler ... [Z] = PhD) as a simple rating graphic, then one concrete everyday task per option ('Is this French correct? -> Haiku'), then what YOU use and one insider tip (e.g. lower effort to save tokens). 60-90 s, an overlay every ~5 s, jargon named once with a plain definition (nima: 'regression = a new change breaks something that worked'). Ideal AI Explained episode shape for a mixed beginner/engineer audience.

pattern: Same news, different payoff: 'a way not many people have tried' + my exact personal workflow shown on screen step by step beats announcing the feature + hype
how_to_apply: Structure: '[TOOL] just [shipped X]. And there's a way of using it not many people have tried that is insanely valuable for [AUDIENCE].' -> 'I used it to build [concrete workflow]' -> steps 1-2-3 as screen recording (top) + face (bottom) with a title bar '[TOOL] FOR [AUDIENCE]' -> name your method -> 2 more use cases -> 'comment [WORD] for the setup'. Counter-evidence in the same week, same format: kallaway's 'ChatGPT can now edit your videos' (news + 'feels like AGI', no workflow) did 0.54x and adamstewart's 'Did OpenAI kill OpenClaw?' did 0.06x. Never ship a release reel without a 'here is what I did with it'.

pattern: Post 2-4 hook/packaging variants of the same idea close together (trial-reel style) and let the winner run - same topic varies 20-90x
how_to_apply: For each AI Explained idea, cut 2-3 versions that differ ONLY in the first 3 s: (a) stat/claim line + title box, (b) question line, (c) visual-first (UI screenshot). Post them as Instagram trial reels (non-followers only) or spaced across the day within the owner's 1-3/day cadence; double down (carousel, follow-up episode) on whichever beats your median by 3x. Evidence: mavgpt 'Honest' prompt 386K vs 4.2K twin, 'Human' prompt 417K vs 4.5K twin; harpercarrollai posted 9 cuts of one Muse video, one hit 92K vs ~2K for the rest.

pattern: Resource list as a fast reel framed against a guilty habit ('watch these instead of brainrot'), each item labelled on screen with its real thumbnail, full list gated behind a comment
how_to_apply: Frame 1: you over a grid of the thumbnails + title '[N]/[N] [videos/repos/courses] to [learn X] instead of [doomscrolling/brainrot]'. Then '#1 [Category]' label top + the thumbnail/screenshot + one-line why (~4 s each, count on fingers), end 'Follow + comment GUIDE + share with a friend'. Pair with the carousel version of the same list (save-bait) the next day. Only 1 creator so far (sabrina_ramonov 6.1x and 3.1x) - test, don't assume.

pattern: Free giveaway behind a comment keyword ('comment EDIT and I'll send you the free skill/prompt/guide') drives comments far above likes on AI tool reels
how_to_apply: Close every tool/explainer reel with 'Follow + comment [ONE WORD tied to the asset] and I'll send you [the free skill / prompt / PDF / repo]'. Make the asset genuinely free and useful (tenfoldmarc's 'edit' reel: 16.9K comments vs 2.5K likes). Needs a DM automation (ManyChat) the owner sets up himself - nothing auto-posts from here. Caveat: flops use it too; it amplifies a good hook, it doesn't rescue a weak one.
